speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा यदभीक्ष्णं निषेवते ।
तदेवापहरत्येनं तस्मात्कल्याणमाचरेत् ॥
iast:
karmaṇā manasā vācā yadabhīkṣṇaṃ niṣevate |
tadevāpaharatyenaṃ tasmātkalyāṇamācaret ||
english: Whatever one repeatedly practises in action, mind and speech, that very thing carries one away; so one should practise what is good.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
मङ्गलालम्भनं योगः श्रुतमुत्थानमार्जवम् ।
भूतिमेतानि कुर्वन्ति सतां चाभीक्ष्ण दर्शनम् ॥
iast:
maṅgalālambhanaṃ yogaḥ śrutamutthānamārjavam |
bhūtimetāni kurvanti satāṃ cābhīkṣṇa darśanam ||
english: Touching auspicious things, discipline, learning, effort, honesty, and often seeing good people: these bring prosperity.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलं दुःखनाशे सुखस्य च ।
महान्भवत्यनिर्विण्णः सुखं चात्यन्तमश्नुते ॥
iast:
anirvedaḥ śriyo mūlaṃ duḥkhanāśe sukhasya ca |
mahānbhavatyanirviṇṇaḥ sukhaṃ cātyantamaśnute ||
english: Not losing heart is the root of fortune, and of happiness when sorrow ends. One who does not lose heart becomes great and enjoys lasting happiness.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
नातः श्रीमत्तरं किं चिदन्यत्पथ्यतमं तथा ।
प्रभ विष्णोर्यथा तात क्षमा सर्वत्र सर्वदा ॥
iast:
nātaḥ śrīmattaraṃ kiṃ cidanyatpathyatamaṃ tathā |
prabha viṣṇoryathā tāta kṣamā sarvatra sarvadā ||
english: For one who is powerful, dear one, there is nothing more glorious and nothing more wholesome than forgiveness, everywhere and always.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
क्षमेदशक्तः सर्वस्य शक्तिमान्धर्मकारणात् ।
अर्थानर्थौ समौ यस्य तस्य नित्यं क्षमा हिता ॥
iast:
kṣamedaśaktaḥ sarvasya śaktimāndharmakāraṇāt |
arthānarthau samau yasya tasya nityaṃ kṣamā hitā ||
english: The powerless should forgive everyone; the powerful should forgive for the sake of dharma. For one to whom gain and loss are the same, forgiveness is always beneficial.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यत्सुखं सेवमानोऽपि धर्मार्थाभ्यां न हीयते ।
कामं तदुपसेवेत न मूढ व्रतमाचरेत् ॥
iast:
yatsukhaṃ sevamāno'pi dharmārthābhyāṃ na hīyate |
kāmaṃ tadupaseveta na mūḍha vratamācaret ||
english: Whatever pleasure one can enjoy without losing dharma or wealth, one may freely enjoy; one should not practise the vow of a fool.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
दुःखार्तेषु प्रमत्तेषु नास्तिकेष्वलसेषु च ।
न श्रीर्वसत्यदान्तेषु ये चोत्साह विवर्जिताः ॥
iast:
duḥkhārteṣu pramatteṣu nāstikeṣvalaseṣu ca |
na śrīrvasatyadānteṣu ye cotsāha vivarjitāḥ ||
english: Fortune does not dwell with those overcome by sorrow, the careless, unbelievers, the lazy, the undisciplined, and those without energy.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
आर्जवेन नरं युक्तमार्जवात्सव्यपत्रपम् ।
अशक्तिमन्तं मन्यन्तो धर्षयन्ति कुबुद्धयः ॥
iast:
ārjavena naraṃ yuktamārjavātsavyapatrapam |
aśaktimantaṃ manyanto dharṣayanti kubuddhayaḥ ||
english: A person who is straightforward and, because of his straightforwardness, modest: the evil-minded think him powerless and attack him.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अत्यार्यमतिदातारमतिशूरमतिव्रतम् ।
प्रज्ञाभिमानिनं चैव श्रीर्भयान्नोपसर्पति ॥
iast:
atyāryamatidātāramatiśūramativratam |
prajñābhimāninaṃ caiva śrīrbhayānnopasarpati ||
english: Fortune, as if out of fear, does not approach one who is too noble, too generous, too brave, too strict in vows, or proud of his wisdom.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अग्निहोत्रफला वेदाः शीलवृत्तफलं श्रुतम् ।
रतिपुत्र फला दारा दत्तभुक्त फलं धनम् ॥
iast:
agnihotraphalā vedāḥ śīlavṛttaphalaṃ śrutam |
ratiputra phalā dārā dattabhukta phalaṃ dhanam ||
english: The fruit of the Vedas is the fire offering; the fruit of learning is good character and conduct; the fruit of a wife is love and sons; the fruit of wealth is giving and enjoying it.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अधर्मोपार्जितैरर्थैर्यः करोत्यौर्ध्व देहिकम् ।
न स तस्य फलं प्रेत्य भुङ्क्तेऽर्थस्य दुरागमात् ॥
iast:
adharmopārjitairarthairyaḥ karotyaurdhva dehikam |
na sa tasya phalaṃ pretya bhuṅkte'rthasya durāgamāt ||
english: One who performs rites for the afterlife with wealth gained unrighteously does not enjoy their fruit after death, because the wealth came by a bad road.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
कानार वनदुर्गेषु कृच्छ्रास्वापत्सु सम्भ्रमे ।
उद्यतेषु च शस्त्रेषु नास्ति शेषवतां भयम् ॥
iast:
kānāra vanadurgeṣu kṛcchrāsvāpatsu sambhrame |
udyateṣu ca śastreṣu nāsti śeṣavatāṃ bhayam ||
english: In wildernesses, forests and fortresses, in hard calamities, in panic, and when weapons are raised, those who have something in reserve have no fear.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
उत्थानं संयमो दाक्ष्यमप्रमादो धृतिः स्मृतिः ।
समीक्ष्य च समारम्भो विद्धि मूलं भवस्य तत् ॥
iast:
utthānaṃ saṃyamo dākṣyamapramādo dhṛtiḥ smṛtiḥ |
samīkṣya ca samārambho viddhi mūlaṃ bhavasya tat ||
english: Effort, self-restraint, skill, attentiveness, steadiness, memory, and starting things after careful thought: know these as the root of prosperity.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
तपोबलं तापसानां ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदां बलम् ।
हिंसा बलमसाधूनां क्षमागुणवतां बलम् ॥
iast:
tapobalaṃ tāpasānāṃ brahma brahmavidāṃ balam |
hiṃsā balamasādhūnāṃ kṣamāguṇavatāṃ balam ||
english: Austerity is the strength of ascetics; Brahman is the strength of those who know Brahman; violence is the strength of the wicked; forgiveness is the strength of the virtuous.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अष्टौ तान्यव्रतघ्नानि आपो मूलं फलं पयः ।
हविर्ब्राह्मण काम्या च गुरोर्वचनमौषधम् ॥
iast:
aṣṭau tānyavrataghnāni āpo mūlaṃ phalaṃ payaḥ |
havirbrāhmaṇa kāmyā ca gurorvacanamauṣadham ||
english: These eight do not break a vow: water, roots, fruit, milk, ghee, what a brahmin wishes, the teacher's word, and medicine.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न तत्परस्य सन्दध्यात्प्रतिकूलं यदात्मनः ।
सङ्ग्रहेणैष धर्मः स्यात्कामादन्यः प्रवर्तते ॥
iast:
na tatparasya sandadhyātpratikūlaṃ yadātmanaḥ |
saṅgraheṇaiṣa dharmaḥ syātkāmādanyaḥ pravartate ||
english: One should not do to another what is disagreeable to oneself. This, in brief, is dharma; other conduct springs from desire.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अक्रोधेन जयेत्क्रोधमसाधुं साधुना जयेत् ।
जयेत्कदर्यं दानेन जयेत्सत्येन चानृतम् ॥
iast:
akrodhena jayetkrodhamasādhuṃ sādhunā jayet |
jayetkadaryaṃ dānena jayetsatyena cānṛtam ||
english: Conquer anger with calm; conquer the wicked with goodness; conquer the miser with giving; and conquer falsehood with truth.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
स्त्री धूर्तकेऽलसे भीरौ चण्डे पुरुषमानिनि ।
चौरे कृतघ्ने विश्वासो न कार्यो न च नास्तिके ॥
iast:
strī dhūrtake'lase bhīrau caṇḍe puruṣamānini |
caure kṛtaghne viśvāso na kāryo na ca nāstike ||
english: Trust should not be placed in a woman, a cheat, a lazy person, a coward, a fierce person, one who boasts of his manliness, a thief, an ungrateful person, or an unbeliever.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अभिवादनशीलस्य नित्यं वृद्धोपसेविनः ।
चत्वारि सम्प्रवर्धन्ते कीर्तिरायुर्यशोबलम् ॥
iast:
abhivādanaśīlasya nityaṃ vṛddhopasevinaḥ |
catvāri sampravardhante kīrtirāyuryaśobalam ||
english: For one who is in the habit of greeting respectfully and always serves the elderly, four things increase: reputation, life, fame and strength.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अतिक्लेशेन येऽर्थाः स्युर्धर्मस्यातिक्रमेण च ।
अरेर्वा प्रणिपातेन मा स्म तेषु मनः कृथाः ॥
iast:
atikleśena ye'rthāḥ syurdharmasyātikrameṇa ca |
arervā praṇipātena mā sma teṣu manaḥ kṛthāḥ ||
english: Gains that come through excessive hardship, by violating dharma, or by bowing down to an enemy: do not set your mind on them.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अविद्यः पुरुषः शोच्यः शोच्यं मिथुनमप्रजम् ।
निराहाराः प्रजाः शोच्याः शोच्यं राष्ट्रमराजकम् ॥
iast:
avidyaḥ puruṣaḥ śocyaḥ śocyaṃ mithunamaprajam |
nirāhārāḥ prajāḥ śocyāḥ śocyaṃ rāṣṭramarājakam ||
english: An uneducated person is to be pitied; a couple without children is to be pitied; people without food are to be pitied; a kingdom without a king is to be pitied.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अध्वा जरा देहवतां पर्वतानां जलं जरा ।
असम्भोगो जरा स्त्रीणां वाक्षल्यं मनसो जरा ॥
iast:
adhvā jarā dehavatāṃ parvatānāṃ jalaṃ jarā |
asambhogo jarā strīṇāṃ vākṣalyaṃ manaso jarā ||
english: Travel is old age for embodied beings; water is old age for mountains; lack of enjoyment is old age for women; harsh words are old age for the mind.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अनाम्नाय मला वेदा ब्राह्मणस्याव्रतं मलम् ।
कौतूहलमला साध्वी विप्रवास मलाः स्त्रियः ॥
iast:
anāmnāya malā vedā brāhmaṇasyāvrataṃ malam |
kautūhalamalā sādhvī vipravāsa malāḥ striyaḥ ||
english: Not reciting is the stain of the Vedas; not keeping vows is the stain of a brahmin; curiosity is the stain of a virtuous woman; living away from home is the stain of women.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सुवर्णस्य मलं रूप्यं रूप्यस्यापि मलं त्रपु ।
ज्ञेयं त्रपु मलं सीसं सीसस्यापि मलं मलम् ॥
iast:
suvarṇasya malaṃ rūpyaṃ rūpyasyāpi malaṃ trapu |
jñeyaṃ trapu malaṃ sīsaṃ sīsasyāpi malaṃ malam ||
english: Silver is the dross of gold, tin the dross of silver; lead is known as the dross of tin, and of lead the dross is dross.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न स्वप्नेन जयेन्निद्रां न कामेन स्त्रियं जयेत् ।
नेन्धनेन जयेदग्निं न पानेन सुरां जयेत् ॥
iast:
na svapnena jayennidrāṃ na kāmena striyaṃ jayet |
nendhanena jayedagniṃ na pānena surāṃ jayet ||
english: One cannot conquer sleep by sleeping, nor a woman by desire, nor fire by fuel, nor liquor by drinking.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यस्य दानजितं मित्रममित्रा युधि निर्जिताः ।
अन्नपानजिता दाराः सफलं तस्य जीवितम् ॥
iast:
yasya dānajitaṃ mitramamitrā yudhi nirjitāḥ |
annapānajitā dārāḥ saphalaṃ tasya jīvitam ||
english: One whose friends are won by gifts, whose enemies are conquered in battle, and whose wives are won by food and drink: his life is fruitful.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सहस्रिणोऽपि जीवन्ति जीवन्ति शतिनस्तथा ।
धृतराष्ट्रं विमुञ्चेच्छां न कथं चिन्न जीव्यते ॥
iast:
sahasriṇo'pi jīvanti jīvanti śatinastathā |
dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ vimuñcecchāṃ na kathaṃ cinna jīvyate ||
english: Those with thousands live, and those with hundreds also live. Give up craving, Dhritarashtra; there is no way one cannot live.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
यत्पृथिव्यां व्रीहि यवं हिरण्यं पशवः स्त्रियः ।
नालमेकस्य तत्सर्वमिति पश्यन्न मुह्यति ॥
iast:
yatpṛthivyāṃ vrīhi yavaṃ hiraṇyaṃ paśavaḥ striyaḥ |
nālamekasya tatsarvamiti paśyanna muhyati ||
english: All the rice, barley, gold, cattle and women on earth are not enough for even one person: one who sees this is not deluded.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
राजन्भूयो ब्रवीमि त्वां पुत्रेषु सममाचर ।
समता यदि ते राजन्स्वेषु पाण्डुसुतेषु च ॥
iast:
rājanbhūyo bravīmi tvāṃ putreṣu samamācara |
samatā yadi te rājansveṣu pāṇḍusuteṣu ca ||
english: King, I tell you again: act equally towards your sons, if you have equal regard, king, for your own sons and the sons of Pandu.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
योऽभ्यर्थितः सद्भिरसज्जमानः
करोत्यर्थं शक्तिमहापयित्वा ।
क्षिप्रं यशस्तं समुपैति सन्तमलं
प्रसन्ना हि सुखाय सन्तः ॥
iast:
yo'bhyarthitaḥ sadbhirasajjamānaḥ
karotyarthaṃ śaktimahāpayitvā |
kṣipraṃ yaśastaṃ samupaiti santamalaṃ
prasannā hi sukhāya santaḥ ||
english: One who, asked by the good, helps them without hesitation and without holding back his strength, quickly gains fame; for the good, when pleased, are able to bring happiness.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
महान्तमप्यर्थमधर्मयुक्तं
यः सन्त्यजत्यनुपाक्रुष्ट एव ।
सुखं स दुःखान्यवमुच्य शेते
जीर्णां त्वचं सर्प इवावमुच्य ॥
iast:
mahāntamapyarthamadharmayuktaṃ
yaḥ santyajatyanupākruṣṭa eva |
sukhaṃ sa duḥkhānyavamucya śete
jīrṇāṃ tvacaṃ sarpa ivāvamucya ||
english: One who gives up even a great gain joined to unrighteousness, without being reproached, sleeps happily, freed from sorrows, like a snake that has shed its old skin.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अनृतं च समुत्कर्षे राजगामि च पैशुनम् ।
गुरोश्चालीक निर्बन्धः समानि ब्रह्महत्यया ॥
iast:
anṛtaṃ ca samutkarṣe rājagāmi ca paiśunam |
guroścālīka nirbandhaḥ samāni brahmahatyayā ||
english: Lying for one's own advancement, slander that reaches the king, and persisting in falsehood towards one's teacher: these are equal to killing a brahmin.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
असूयैक पदं मृत्युरतिवादः श्रियो वधः ।
अशुश्रूषा त्वरा श्लाघा विद्यायाः शत्रवस्त्रयः ॥
iast:
asūyaika padaṃ mṛtyurativādaḥ śriyo vadhaḥ |
aśuśrūṣā tvarā ślāghā vidyāyāḥ śatravastrayaḥ ||
english: Envy is one step from death; excessive talk is the killer of fortune. Not listening, hurry and self-praise are the three enemies of learning.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या नास्ति विद्यार्थिनः सुखम् ।
सुखार्थी वा त्यजेद्विद्यां विद्यार्थी वा सुखं त्यजेत् ॥
iast:
sukhārthinaḥ kuto vidyā nāsti vidyārthinaḥ sukham |
sukhārthī vā tyajedvidyāṃ vidyārthī vā sukhaṃ tyajet ||
english: Where is learning for one who seeks comfort? There is no comfort for one who seeks learning. Let the comfort-seeker give up learning, or the learner give up comfort.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
नाग्निस्तृप्यति काष्ठानां नापगानां महोदधिः ।
नान्तकः सर्वभूतानां न पुंसां वामलोचना ॥
iast:
nāgnistṛpyati kāṣṭhānāṃ nāpagānāṃ mahodadhiḥ |
nāntakaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ na puṃsāṃ vāmalocanā ||
english: Fire is never satisfied with logs, nor the great ocean with rivers, nor death with all beings, nor a beautiful-eyed woman with men.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
आशा धृतिं हन्ति समृद्धिमन्तकः
क्रोधः श्रियं हन्ति यशः कदर्यता ।
अपालनं हन्ति पशूंश्च राजन्न्
एकः क्रुद्धो ब्राह्मणो हन्ति राष्ट्रम् ॥
iast:
āśā dhṛtiṃ hanti samṛddhimantakaḥ
krodhaḥ śriyaṃ hanti yaśaḥ kadaryatā |
apālanaṃ hanti paśūṃśca rājann
ekaḥ kruddho brāhmaṇo hanti rāṣṭram ||
english: Craving destroys steadiness; death destroys prosperity; anger destroys fortune; miserliness destroys fame; neglect destroys cattle, king; and one angry brahmin destroys a kingdom.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अजश्च कांस्यं च रथश्च नित्यं
मध्वाकर्षः शकुनिः श्रोत्रियश् च ।
वृद्धो ज्ञातिरवसन्नो वयस्य
एतानि ते सन्तु गृहे सदैव ॥
iast:
ajaśca kāṃsyaṃ ca rathaśca nityaṃ
madhvākarṣaḥ śakuniḥ śrotriyaś ca |
vṛddho jñātiravasanno vayasya
etāni te santu gṛhe sadaiva ||
english: Goats, bronze, a chariot, honey, a bird, a Vedic scholar, an aged relative and a friend fallen on hard times: may these always be in your house.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अजोक्षा चन्दनं वीणा आदर्शो मधुसर्पिषी ।
विषमौदुम्बरं शङ्खः स्वर्णं नाभिश्च रोचना ॥
iast:
ajokṣā candanaṃ vīṇā ādarśo madhusarpiṣī |
viṣamaudumbaraṃ śaṅkhaḥ svarṇaṃ nābhiśca rocanā ||
english: A goat and a bull, sandalwood, a lute, a mirror, honey and ghee, poison-curing fig wood, a conch, gold, musk and yellow pigment:

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
गृहे स्थापयितव्यानि धन्यानि मनुरब्रवीत् ।
देव ब्राह्मण पूजार्थमतिथीनां च भारत ॥
iast:
gṛhe sthāpayitavyāni dhanyāni manurabravīt |
deva brāhmaṇa pūjārthamatithīnāṃ ca bhārata ||
english: Manu said these auspicious things should be kept in the house, for the worship of gods and brahmins and for guests, Bharata.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
इदं च त्वां सर्वपरं ब्रवीमि
पुण्यं पदं तात महाविशिष्टम् ।
न जातु कामान्न भयान्न लोभाद्
धर्मं त्यजेज्जीवितस्यापि हेतोः ॥
iast:
idaṃ ca tvāṃ sarvaparaṃ bravīmi
puṇyaṃ padaṃ tāta mahāviśiṣṭam |
na jātu kāmānna bhayānna lobhād
dharmaṃ tyajejjīvitasyāpi hetoḥ ||
english: And this I tell you, above all, dear one, the holy and supreme principle: never abandon dharma out of desire, fear or greed, not even for the sake of life.
